text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States intervenes, and Russia warns Turkey not to attempt to escalate tension in Cyprus.
- The silence of Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash about President Glafcos Clerides's proposal for demilitarisation talks is prolonging tension on the island.
- British tourists claim their tour operators sent them to spend their holiday at a brothel on the island.
- Saints cured my leg, says refugee, aged 81.
- The United Nations peacekeeping force refused to countersign the results of a Turkish investigation into the shooting of a Turkish soldier at his sentry post.
- Nicosia and Athens deny any knowledge of movements by the Turkish occupation troops suggesting further aggression in Cyprus.
- Bill giving 18-year-olds right to vote goes to parliament.
- Turkey attempts to put pressure on Cyprus to cancel its armament programmes and scupper EU negotiation talks by making threats of an imminent attack.
- Murderers of a pub owner killed in a bomb explosion last week are Bulgarian contract killers.
- Children who were ill with viral meningitis are being barred from several schools.

- The United States is playing a double game, to have the government stop its armanents and to drag us into a dialogue, by spreading rumours on Turkish intentions to sink a vessel bringing tanks for the national guard.
- Staff at the Accounting Office of the government will go on a 48-hour strike on Thursday.
